pairs.subject: ui-controls
pairs.evidence: examples/atlas/components/atlas/chrome/Claims.tsx:74 Each claim's full statement is shown only through the native title attribute on the lens-rail button. The standard names that attribute as a tooltip temptation signature: there is no delay, keyboard or touch cannot reach it, and essential content is hidden behind hover. A grep found the claim text rendered nowhere else in the UI; the only other use is the agent tool read.ts:159.

techniques.evidence: examples/atlas/components/atlas/Mast.tsx:225 The [ / ] keyboard shortcut is documented only in a native title on a span that cannot take focus. Claims.tsx:74 and Mast.tsx:124 (title={v.blurb}) do the same, giving 7 title= uses in the context's TSX. The tooltip contract says a tooltip is never the only carrier of essential information and that a native title is not a tooltip.

examples/atlas/components/atlas/Mast.tsx:60 The segmented switchers build on the kit's roving-focus behaviour primitive and do not re-implement the arrow-key logic. Pane.tsx:71 does the same with the kit's useOverlayEscape. This is wrapping, not forking, at the behaviour layer.

examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/Shell.tsx:357 None of the context's components (Mast, Claims, Pane, AtlasTools) accepts a className or style passthrough, and call sites pass only data and handlers. The precondition (a shared control with a styling passthrough) does not hold here.
